canonical_statement: Let M be a connected finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold. If its induced Riemannian distance is a complete metric, then for every p and q in M there is a geodesic segment from p to q whose length equals the Riemannian distance from p to q.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: a type M in an explicit universe, a finite-dimensional smooth manifold structure and Riemannian metric; exact scalar, model-with-corners, regularity, topology, and distance instances are not yet selected
ordered_binders: finite-dimensional real model space and manifold/model-with-corners structure
hypotheses: the metric induced by the Riemannian structure is complete
conclusion: There exists a geodesic segment from p to q that realizes the Riemannian distance.

alternate_encodings.relationship: classically equivalent under the standard finite-dimensional connected Riemannian hypotheses

alternate_encodings.target: every closed bounded subset is compact
alternate_encodings.relationship: properness formulation in the Hopf-Rinow equivalence family

alternate_encodings.target: the exponential map at a point is defined on the whole tangent space and is surjective
alternate_encodings.relationship: classical global exponential-map formulation with hypotheses and conventions still to audit

degenerate_case_policy: Connectedness is explicit. The p = q case, empty and singleton manifolds, dimension zero, disconnected spaces, boundary conventions, and weak/infinite-dimensional metrics must be mutation-tested before statement acceptance.
foundation_profile: rev-5.6 profile not yet instantiated; classical choice, quotient, manifold, and completeness assumptions remain open
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel plus pinned mathlib intended; exact versions and transitive closure remain open
